Does anyone here have any experience with these guitars? I have had nothing but great experiences with them and am keen to hear others stories - good or bad.
Mostly good--especially with the Japanese Squiers. That said, the Japanese strats with the System I Tremolo (vibrato, really) has sort of a love-it-or-hate-it thing going on.

I own two Contemporary Strats and one Contemporary Tele with the sys1 trems. I agree with the love it or hate it thing.

The bridges are great... its the nuts that suck ass. Usually, by this time, people lose or throw away the parts. Last Strat I bought, I had to fabricate the parts by hand. Lame. BUT once I got it right, they stay in tune really well.

Fun fact... the "Squiers" and the "Fenders" are the same exact guitars, just different decals on the headstock. Same electronics, bodies, necks and hardware.

I don't have any experience with 80's MIJ Fenders, but I have a mid-2000's Tele from Japan (the '62 reissue model), and it has both beautiful tone and fantastically smooth finish to the neck. Feels better than any other guitar I've gotten to play on so far, including friends' expensive Gibsons.

I almost want to say Japanese Fenders always hit the mark as far a quality and workmanship. Definitely a step above the Mexican stuff they are building and I would venture to say that they are better then the entry level USA Fenders.

I read here that they are ceasing operations. BOO.
Yeah, I heard about that and it's only made me more convinced that this MIJ Tele is going to be my main guitar for life.

I've never owned a Japanese fender but my first nice guitar was a Line6 Variax 700.

It got stolen in a break in :( but I eventually managed to replace it with another one off eBay (hard tail this time)

Both were very solid, well built instruments that are a pleasure to play and it's my go to guitar to grab and play.

Why is this relevant? My understanding is that these guitars (the 700 variax) were made in the same Japanese factory as the fenders you refer to.

Speaking of Japanese guitars I also have an old busted up Vantage LP clone made in the Matsumoto factory and those are also a good MIJ guitar to snag (anything from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsumoku

tl;dr the Japanese make good guitars, because they love their rock and roll.
They were definitely made there. And your TL;DR sums it up. Thanks!!

KInd've. I have an old Univox Ripper (1977~). It's a Stratocaster with 3 double humbuckers. In the late 70's and 80's the Japanese put together some really cool frankenstein Fenders at the now famous Matsumoku factory. These are not the weird Japanese Teiscos you see around, these are more often the weird Japanese Fanders and Epiphones you see around. I love my Japenese Strat for its ridiculous 3 double humbuckers and decent construction. I found it on ebay for $600. I set itup for 5 strings C-G-D-G-C. It's a low tuning to take advantage of the 3 hi-output double humbuckers' warm & deep characteristics...hoping for some nasty breakup and natural distortion.
